cards.explanation: The answer is David's thoughts. David says, "You understand my thoughts from afar." Your thoughts are the one room you figure nobody can walk into. The LORD doesn't need to come any closer to understand them. I think David is amazed by that, and I'd be too.

The answer is False. David says, "Even before a word is on my tongue, You know all about it, O LORD." The words haven't even left his tongue yet. That's a lot of knowing, friends, and I can't even guess what I'm about to say before I say it.

The answer is that he can't fully take it in. David says, "Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too lofty for me to attain." It's too big for him to reach. I think he's standing there amazed, like a guy staring up at the tallest oven he's ever seen.

The answer is True. David says, "If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there." Sheol is the realm of the dead, so he's naming the highest place and the deepest place. The LORD is there in both. That's a lot of ground covered, friends.
The answer is True. David says, "…even there Your hand will guide me; Your right hand will hold me fast." So even at the farthest sea, he isn't alone out there. He gets guided and held.

The answer is that night is as bright as day to God. David says, "…even the darkness is not dark to You, but the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to You." So if David hoped the dark would hide him, it wouldn't. God sees there like it's noon.

The answer is that he praises God. David says, "I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made." Just before that, he says God formed his inmost being and knit him together in his mother's womb. He looks at how he was made and what comes out of him is praise.

The answer is False. David says, "My frame was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, when I was woven together in the depths of the earth." It was made in secret, but God saw all of it. No part of David was hidden from Him.

The answer is False. David says, "all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be." Not one of them had started yet, and they were already written down. So the book came first, and the living came after.

The answer is many. David says, "…how vast is their sum!" and then, "If I were to count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand…" Think about counting a whole beach, and then there's still more. That's how vast God's thoughts are, friends.

The answer is that David asks God to slay them. David says, "O God, that You would slay the wicked…" This is a heavy part of the psalm, and I won't dress it up. He asks it of God, and I think he says it with strong feelings.
The answer is False. David says they "…speak of You deceitfully…" So their words about God aren't honest. He adds, "Your enemies take Your name in vain."
The answer is True. David says, "See if there is any offensive way in me…" He asks God to look. I'd sooner hide a burnt batch under a dish towel, but David asks.

The answer is in the way that lasts forever. David says, "lead me in the way everlasting." He starts the psalm with God searching him, and he ends it asking God to lead him. I think that's a good way to finish, friends.
